en: Blood from a single fist covered his eye,
Such was Bilgich’s wisdom,
He had ridden upon the throne,
Bilgich had laid up treasure,
In his eyes no soul remained but Bermet,
Right there was the ground,
When the moon remained between them,
No man could match the lion,
What opened was ordained by God,
He truly turned it into an open plain,
Life departed under the force of his valor,
He was a warrior like the blue spear-tip,
After striking, his strength left him in exhaustion.
From the rank and spoils he had gained,
They devised a stratagem against him,
They struck his glasslike eyes,
What remained of his mouth,
His own fierce bearing took his life,
One who came as his equal,
Struck by Heaven, he stopped,
Leading him in the Turkish manner,
They became locked in combat,
When they took the road, a clamor arose,
Would he draw in the horse’s reins?
Knowing nothing of his own life,
Would he not sacrifice himself for great Beijing?
One side of great Beijing,
One side of the border mountain,
You look out toward the desert,
The great sun rose behind them,
He had words to tell in sorrow,
At that word there was a stubborn hero,
Heaven struck the stubborn one,
Those who met were truly equal,
The champion’s bravery,
Was not greater than mine,
When they went into that desert,
Let me drive out his demon in the desert,
This lone Joltoy,
Let me put a complete end to him,
Even the noble ones were many like this.
Thus spoke Chong Bilgich,
His mind worked as he devised a plan,
He attacked in many different ways,
His fearsome presence was grim,
He drove warrior Joltoy onward,
Who had ever seen such wrath?
He sought a plan for every side,
His head reeled as he overturned them,
Taking one of them, he staggered,
Upon the steed beneath him,
He turned its head toward Beijing,
A snowy place blinded the eyes,
Now he reduced the foe in his hands,
Numerous as mighty Jadyger’s men,
Finding a place where rain would fall,
Circling three times, he struck three times,
Leaving none of the Kalmyks behind,
All of it against the Chinese,
They fought while circling,
The boar struck by Heaven,
Flowing from the sky, it fell to earth,
Looking at it, one could not understand its nature,
It would indeed remain wingless,
Their sight darkened and their souls were bound,
When they looked, Bilgich had escaped from thousands.
When the wind struck through the fog,
While their eyes remained blinded,
Ak Joltoy came out behind them,
Without a hair being harmed,
The enemy stood beneath the moon,
With the enemy pursuing from behind,
Chong Bilgich let out a battle cry,
It was the time when he survived,
Like lion-hearted Joltoy,
Unable to withstand his ferocity,
It was when the multitude remained,
We used to see the mortal hero,
It was the time when he wrought destruction,
The man watched and grew wrathful,
It was the time to destroy his eyes,
The falcon cried out beneath the sun,
It was the moment to wound him,
Each day he spared not even forty,
It was the time to cast them onto the plain,
The wrathful man advanced,
The remaining creature was wretched,
None of its abundant blood remained,
Its red life was cut off,
The poor host was destroyed,
It was the time to attack them face to face,
The great stubborn warrior drove off the gray ones,
His eye was fixed upon the warrior,
Fulfilling what he had wished,
When he reached that desert.
One pursued the other,
To capture Ak Joltoy,
The distant wasteland,
For this Joltoy to remain,
Now the boar was formidable,
Chong Bilgich had become overwhelming,
He was taken away from the people,
Chong Bilgich had fled,
When Bilgich took his people,
Just then Ak Joltoy,
Placed the saddle behind him,
The poor man who had gone to paradise,
Let me drive them as far as Beijing,
You shall see the whole of it,
Let me drive them into the darkness,
He sat there for a long while,
Let me take my turn now,
Casting him into filth, they raised a clamor,
Let me leave him with his coat open,
Such a deed against the Kyrgyz,
The boar who had gone to paradise,
Let me pursue him all the way to Beijing,
If I catch him, I shall seize him with both hands,
Thus spoke Ak Joltoy.
The fleeing Bilgich invoked his spell,
Kunan-Sur beneath him,
Whistled like a drawn bowstring,
Like a black stone striking a fox,
He roared like iron,
He pressed the steed’s flank with his heels,
Circling ahead, he pursued him,
Behold the land none could reach,
Crossing seven mountain spurs,
Beginning the direct assault,
The dark eyes of the two spirits,
Circling along twelve roads,
Not even thirty days remained,
Ak Joltoy’s pursuit caught up,
Chong Bilgich tired from fleeing,
The steed beneath him,
In the dark hour, like a pale mare,
Its tail lashed against its body,
A mount meant for a fleeing enemy,
If Kunan pursued, it would not escape,
He himself was the child of the sun,
The warrior behind him flew forward,
Lengthening the distant road,
The pangs of hunger subsided,
When he went after him across the ridge,
Kunan-Sur strained its back,
He came close to Bilgich.
He drew close to his land,
As though striking from a high pass,
Into the torrent of the ravine,
It flowed smoothly onward,
The sun’s heat drove a great storm,
His broad back slipped,
He continued down the road,
Before thousands whose eyes were blinded,
Toward the ravine filled to overflowing,
It was a place like a boundary marker,
Unable to settle upon the land,
Saying the high bank was nearer,
Saying his grief had bent him double,
Saying he was Kokosu himself,
Of iron-souled Bilgich,
Saying, “Now my fist is my eye,”
Preparing himself to see it,
Strength flowed through his body,
The hero’s spirit did not rest,
Never lagging behind,
He would strike Beijing, which had raised the turmoil,
The great man’s spirit did not rest,
Casting the enemy down in disgrace,
Saying his waist would break if it slipped,
He carried out what he had said,
The army’s spirit did not rest.
The followers became a people,
The warrior’s courage was firm,
His sight failed, poor soul,
His soul showed no mercy to the foe,
Show your prowess, champion Ak Joltoy,
Dear souls, Kunan-Sur,
Though it came even from the moon, it was a beast,
Thinking far ahead, he thundered,
It burst apart like embers,
He was about to be questioned,
His mouth was broad as a ship,
The true steed surged forward,
Thundering as before,
A gray trail streamed behind him,
His windblown tail whirled,
Running headlong toward the ravine,
Ak Joltoy of the sixty champions,
Now he too was a warrior of paradise,
The claim arising from a great deed,
Kumar did not fall to the ground,
Saying, “May the Creator Himself protect us,”
His strength came with red fury,
The sword hilt became his support,
Without stopping, he caught up,
Bilgich fell like a mountain,
Biting hard where no hold seemed possible,
He looked upward, saying the Creator was his shield.
Dwelling there like a mountain gate,
Fixing his gaze like a lion,
Dragging by the tail, he pressed it down,
Its mouth opened with difficulty,
Holding the spear before his brow,
He brought it down and struck,
Saying, “May the Creator be my companion and shield,”
When the spear struck their horses,
The wrathful hero Joltoy,
Wielding two spears,
Like a creature with fists of stone,
Of Bilgich who thrust the spear,
The champions recognized it,
Their coats split across the waist,
This hero strained with all his might,
The champion’s quality became evident,
Thrusting the spear countless times,
This time, champion Joltoy,
Fell and was thrown down,
Strength left his body,
His foot slipped from the stirrup,
The reins slipped from his hand,
From the warhorse’s neck,
His two eyes rolled,
His life truly departed into the sand,
He stared like granulated sugar,
While Bilgich stood among thousands,
The fame of his spear remained.
[They were the burning ones themselves],
Joltoy, who had come alone,
It was time to attack him together.
Truly, Joltoy's anger,
[It was time for it to remain],
[One gust of your elder's fury],
It was time to encounter it.
God grant that we never see it,
[The warrior split right through],
The oppressor standing on the road,
[Never sated at a funeral feast],
Sparing no life when they swarmed,
Ninety-four had come to the fight,
Marksmen who drew bows,
Warriors like devouring monsters,
Who attacked together at a command,
A person's nose and ears,
When angered, the crafty infidel,
Wore them as amulets.
He himself was an intelligent man,
[Yet more foolish than a beast when speaking],
Unable to find a way, he submitted.
[From the people who ate and drank],
Tested and come from Beijing,
They were the chosen ones themselves.
[Gathering a throng by trickery],
Against Joltoy, who chased Bilgich,
[A huge, potbellied childlike brute],
It was time to bring it down.
